Objectives of the activity

The subject of the PSE S.A. activity is to provide the services ofelectricity transmission in compliance with the required criteria of the security of the Polish Power System operation.The main objectives of the PSE S.A. activity are:- providing electricity transmission services and ensuring secure and cost-effective operation of the Polish Power System whilst meeting the conditions of synchronous operation with other European systems,
- ensuring the necessary development of the domestic transmission grid and cross-border interconnections,
- making transmission capacity available on market based methods for cross-border exchange purposes,
- creating the technical infrastructure for the operation of the domestic wholesale electricity market.

Role and ResponsibilitiesWithin the responsibilities specified in the Energy Law Act (art. 9c par 2) the transmission system operator:- contributes to the security of electricity supply by ensuring security of the power system operation and adequate transmission capacity,
- provides the operation of the transmission system in an effective manner whilstensuring the required reliability and quality of supply and in cooperation with Distribution System Operators - in the coordinatedpart of the 110 kV network,
- maintains the transmission system, including interconnections with other power systems, in a manner which ensures reliable operation of the power system,
- ensures the long-term ability of the power system to meet reasonable domestic and cross-border demands for the transmission of electricity, including development of the transmission power system, and, where appropriate, development of interconnections with other power systems,
- cooperates with other transmission system operators and energy enterprises in order to ensure reliabe and effective operation of the power systems and to coordinate their development,
- dispatches the generation units connected to the transmission grid and the generation units of the installed capacity equal to or more than 50 MW, connected to the coordinated part of the 110 kV network with due regard to the contracts with the transmission system users and technical constraints in the system,
- manages congestion on the interconnections with other systems,
- purchases the ancillary services and provides system services necessary for the secure, reliable and efficient electricity system functioning,
- balances the power system, including the service of the imbalance settlement of system users,
- manages electricity flows in the transmission system and in cooperation with Distribution System Operators - in the coordinated 110 kV network,
- purchases electricity to cover the transmission losses, with due observation of transparent and non-discriminatory market-based procedures,
- provides system users and other interconnected transmission system operators with the information necessary for the access to and use of the transmission network, regarding conditions for transmission services, including in relation to the cross-border exchange of electricity, network operation and balancing,
- prepares the power system defence and restoration plans,
- exercises power supply restrictions imposed in line with the laws and regulations in force.

Independent research and consulting enterprise specializing in atmospheric optics, light pollution science, satellite remote sensing, and dark sky preservation. The company provides scientific expertise in quantifying artificial light at night impacts, developing light management strategies, and supporting International Dark Sky Place certifications.
Core competencies include: light pollution measurement and modeling, all-sky photometry, atmospheric radiative transfer, satellite data analysis (VIIRS DNB) for radiance trend assessment and urban planning applications, space debris impact assessment on astronomical observations, and development of evidence-based lighting policies for protected areas and municipalities.
The principal investigator brings extensive experience from dual affiliations with the Slovak Academy of Sciences and the University of Vienna's Institute for Astrophysics, with proven track record in EU-funded research (Marie Curie fellowship, INTERREG Central Europe projects) and leadership roles in international astronomical organizations (IAU working groups, DarkSky International). Demonstrated expertise in processing and analyzing satellite nighttime imagery for temporal radiance trend development and supporting municipal lighting planning initiatives.
Services offered: scientific consulting for lighting projects, satellite-based light pollution assessments, environmental impact assessments for artificial light, dark sky certification support, light pollution monitoring network design and implementation, expert reports for public authorities, and capacity building in sustainable outdoor lighting practices.
Relevant project experience includes establishment of Europe's largest regional light pollution monitoring network, scientific leadership of Austria's first International Dark Sky Park certification, VIIRS DNB-based radiance analyses for city planning authorities, and research publications in high-impact journals (Science, Nature Astronomy) on light pollution and space sustainability topics.

SeedFence is a cybersecurity company focused on securing embedded systems, founded in 2023 by a highly experienced team.
SeedFence has developped an on-premises and cloud-based eXtended Detection & Response (XDR) platform designed for Android smartphones and embedded systems.The platform relies on lightweight XDR agents that is flexible enough to be deployed on many embedded devices and a centralized management system that can be hosted either in the cloud or on-premises, including within highly sensitive environments. 
SeedFence’s cutting-edge XDR technology is boosted by AI and is designed to detect, analyze, and block cyberattacks targeting Android devices, as well as IoT and Operational Technology (OT) systems.
While smartphones are often treated as closed or opaque systems, SeedFence aims to deliver best-in-class security for Android devices while providing unprecedented visibility into Android’s internal behavior.
Beyond smartphones, SeedFence’s XDR platform addresses the specific constraints of IoT and OT environments, offering a highly flexible solution adapted to a wide range of systems such as satellites, defense platforms, electric vehicle charging stations, and railway systems.

Together with its partner Thales, SeedFence has recently won a contract with CNES to deploy one of the very first satellite-based cyber detection solutions in France and Europe, following a public call for tenders.

Global Space Services Technologies AB (GSST) is a Swedish space technology company focused on the development and operation of ground segment infrastructure and services for satellite missions. The company provides ground station services, system integration, and related technologies supporting satellite missions, with a current focus on polar and high-latitude operations.

GSST develops and operates ground station infrastructure in northern Sweden, optimized for near-polar and sun-synchronous orbits, and offers Ground Station as a Service (GSaaS), antenna hosting, and mission support services across the full mission lifecycle, including Launch and Early Orbit Phase (LEOP) and routine operations. The company also works with regulatory processes, spectrum licensing, and operational integration to enable secure and reliable satellite communications.

In addition to operational services, GSST is engaged in technology development related to satellite communications, ground segment automation, simulation tools, and future ground infrastructure concepts. This includes work on communication system simulation, mission preparation tools, and scalable architectures for next-generation satellite systems.

GSS collaborates with commercial, institutional, and governmental stakeholders and is actively expanding its international footprint, including planned activities in Southeast Asia, while maintaining its core operational base in Sweden. The company aims to contribute to a resilient and competitive European space ecosystem by enabling accessible, flexible, and high-quality ground segment solutions for emerging and established satellite operators.

benntec Systemtechnik GmbH is a German technology company specializing in the development of digital training systems, immersive simulation environments, and operational Digital Twins for complex and safety-critical domains. For more than 30 years, the company has designed and implemented customized digital training solutions that support effective, reproducible, and operationally relevant education and training in environments characterized by high system complexity and stringent reliability requirements.
Headquartered in Bremen, with an additional site in Rostock (Warnemünde), benntec employs more than 120 interdisciplinary specialists with expertise in learning sciences, instructional design, software engineering, simulation technologies, system development, and project management. The company combines didactic methodology with deep system understanding and high-fidelity digital representations to enable sustainable knowledge transfer and procedural competence.
benntec develops practice-oriented, system-centric training environments that prepare users for real operational contexts. Its solutions range from computer- and web-based training and SCORM-compliant e-learning modules to desktop simulations, mobile learning and maintenance applications, and integrated blended learning architectures supported by learning management systems.
A central focus is the integration of immersive Extended Reality technologies, including Virtual Reality, Augmented Reality, and Mixed Reality, with operational Digital Twins. These Digital Twins are designed for training purposes and represent system architecture, internal structures, functional relationships, and dynamic system states. This enables users to explore cause–effect relationships, subsystem interactions, and off-nominal behavior beyond externally observable system states.
Building on extensive experience in mission-critical operational domains, benntec develops multi-user XR training ecosystems supporting supervised and self-paced training for maintenance, operational, and contingency procedures. Scenario configuration, disturbance injection, real-time system-state visualization, and structured debriefing are integral components. Training can be conducted entirely in virtual environments, reducing dependence on physical mock-ups while improving scalability and repeatability.
benntec is a long-standing supplier to German and international defense organizations and collaborates closely with the defense industry. This background has shaped a strong focus on robustness, traceability, security, and process reliability. The underlying methodologies and technologies are transferable to spaceflight-related applications, including astronaut training, mission operations, and systems engineering, where deep system understanding and precise procedural execution are critical.
The company operates under a certified quality management system in accordance with DIN EN ISO 9001:2015.

Munster Technological University (MTU) is a multi-campus public university located in the south of Ireland, established in 2021 with over 18,000 learners and a growing research ecosystem with an annual expenditure of greater than �33m. A defining feature of the university is its strong emphasis on applied learning, industry collaboration, and practice-based education, ensuring graduates are well prepared for real-world careers.
Research is a core pillar of MTU’s mission, with active research centres focusing on areas such as advanced manufacturing, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, sustainable energy, biotechnology, and smart maritime technologies. Researchers at MTU collaborate with international universities, space agencies, and industry partners on projects related to Earth observation, space systems engineering, and emerging space technologies.
